meta.title: Dispatch feasibility fixture matrix, refs #146
meta.status: ILLUSTRATIVE DESIGN EXPECTATIONS for ACCEPTED DESIGN contracts A1-A6 and the object-set rule (operator-accepted; design only, NOT implemented). Not executable feature tests, not a conformance measurement, not measured readiness, not host facts. All identifiers, digests and values are synthetic. Acceptance authorizes no evaluator/consumption implementation (gate G8 not started; B2 separately gated; provider, matcher and isolation gates unresolved).
meta.shape_status: Two shapes coexist. (1) ACCEPTED SCHEMA BASELINE: 'proposals.proposed_schema_baseline' (closed fact value objects, 15 fact keys incl. artifact_contract and authority_decision); the 'proposals' group key is kept only for traceability to PR #170. (2) LEGACY ILLUSTRATIVE SUMMARY SHAPE: top-level 'baseline' (published vector B envelope plus a prose capability_snapshot_summary) and 'cases'/'combined_failures'. The legacy shape is NOT executable under the accepted schemas (facts are prose, not closed value objects; artifact_contract and authority_decision are absent). Legacy case ids are kept only for traceability; their expected reasons arrays use the accepted 13-check expansion where an expansion applies, and the entries listed in 'superseded_illustrative_expectations' record what changed.
meta.superseded_illustrative_expectations: Pre-acceptance expansion arrays listed the 11-check snapshot_derived list (no authority.reference entry except via authority_unverified in unverified_provenance, and no contract.artifact entry). They are superseded by the 13-check list in these legacy cases: stale_epoch, wrong_slot, task_and_capability_both_expired, unverified_provenance (authority_unverified unchanged; contract.artifact added), combined_stale_denial_is_not_denial, combined_stale_epoch_and_task_expiry. Also superseded: any reading of a legacy case where binding.schema fails (A5: malformed input throws; binding.schema is pass in every returned report) and allowed_small_task as feasible under the legacy summary (the accepted baseline additionally needs known artifact_contract and a bound authority_decision).
meta.encoding: MCTL-CJ1 (see design doc section 4). Digests here are symbolic labels, except where a case cites design vector B.
meta.snapshot_derived_checks_note: Accepted list of exactly 13 (A3 added contract.artifact after ownership.files; A4 added authority.reference first). Never included: the seven binding.* checks and estimate.advisory.
meta.reasons_semantics: reasons[] is an ORDERED array (not a set, no encoder sort/dedup). Entry = 'check_id:code', one per (check, code) with a non-pass status. Total order = (class rank, check order, code bytewise ascending). Class rank: binding 0, unauthorized 1, blocked_dependency 2, needs_split 3, busy 4, uncertain 5. A reason's class: binding.* -> binding; status fail -> the check's section 5 class; status unknown/absent/stale -> uncertain. ACCEPTED EXCEPTION (A3): for ownership.files each reason has its own class (ownership_conflict, worktree_dirty -> blocked_dependency; ownership_unknown, worktree_unknown -> uncertain) even when the check status is fail. The order is NOT ascending by whole string. For consumption results the class is 'consumption' for every entry, then consumption_check_order, then code.
meta.not_evaluable_rule: When binding fails because the snapshot is untrusted or not about this task (provenance unverified, other slot, other epoch), every snapshot_derived_checks item (13) is status unknown with code evidence_not_evaluable, except authority.reference when provenance is unverified: it is unknown with authority_unverified (its own entry, not repeated). When the snapshot is verified and for this slot/epoch but outside its freshness window, every one of the 13 is status stale with code evidence_stale. Not-evaluable wins if both apply. A schema-invalid snapshot is not an expansion case: it is an input error (A5), no report. Each such check appears exactly once in reasons[] (an explicit reason for it IS its entry). No such check is ever pass or fail. In every case below these entries are written out in full, in check_order; there is no placeholder token.
meta.closed_reason_codes_note: Closed code set: see design doc 13.8. Includes dependency_unknown, fixture_unknown, artifact_evidence_unknown, artifact_contract_mismatch, worktree_dirty, worktree_unknown, ownership_unknown, authority_unverified, authority_evidence_mismatch, authority_denied, report_not_evaluable. path_pattern_unsupported and authority_applicability_unknown belong to NOT SELECTED alternatives and are not accepted codes.
meta.expectation_reading: check_status_overrides lists only checks that differ from the all-pass baseline. A case's expected.verdict, binding_valid and reasons are the full expected result. 'mutation' may also override evaluated_at_ms or snapshot fields; the baseline snapshot window ends at 1789999900000 and the envelope expires at 1790000000000.

baseline.status: LEGACY ILLUSTRATIVE SUMMARY SHAPE, kept for traceability of stable case ids. The envelope is valid under the accepted schemas (design vector B, bytes and digest unchanged). The capability_snapshot_summary is prose and is NOT a valid accepted-schema snapshot (not executable); the accepted-schema baseline is proposals.proposed_schema_baseline.
baseline.description: Small allowed task. All required checks pass. Envelope is design vector B (sha256 43e77d4fafa97cc56fe831d1bdcb145468f821b940bdf1519a074157c9527880).

facts.mandatory_writes: known (independent verified source): [docs/example-146.md], lower bound 1, inside allowed_files

cases.description: Baseline: every required check passes, binding valid.
allowed_files contains a path matching a verified forbidden pattern in the known path_policy.
cases.mutation: envelope.allowed_files = ["secrets/example.txt"]; snapshot path_policy known and forbids secrets/**; mandatory_writes = [secrets/example.txt]

cases.description: Envelope slot_epoch 7 but the snapshot describes epoch 8: the slot was re-registered. The snapshot is not about this slot incarnation, so its facts are not evaluable.
Snapshot describes a different slot than the envelope names.
Verified fresh slot_state says the slot has an inflight task.
attempts_seen already contains this attempt_id.
cases.note: Substantive evidence is individually evaluable here, so those checks stay pass and are retained under invalid binding; the report is still not feasible.

cases.description: Base moved since the envelope bound base_sha.
cases.mutation: snapshot.facts.repo_base = known: head differs from bound base_sha

cases.description: A required fixture/test-data id is known to be unavailable.
No permission profile in the snapshot, so command decisions cannot be tied to one.
The real matcher (future provider) decided a required command is denied. B1 does not evaluate the matcher; it consumes the decision.
Another owner holds a claim overlapping allowed_files.
cases.mutation: snapshot.facts.ownership = known: overlapping claim by another owner

cases.description: Snapshot carries OS identity and repo base facts with status absent / unknown (keys present, no value); this is not an omitted-key schema error.
cases.note: Missing identity or base can never produce feasible.

cases.description: Only the envelope has expired: evaluated_at_ms is after envelope expires_at_ms, but the snapshot window was extended so the snapshot is still fresh at that clock value. Facts remain individually evaluable and are retained as pass.

With the unmodified baseline snapshot (window ends 1789999900000), evaluated_at_ms 1790000000001 is after BOTH the snapshot and the envelope expiry. Two binding checks fail; every snapshot-derived check is stale, never pass.
cases.note: binding.capability_fresh (rank: binding, check order 5) precedes binding.not_expired (check order 6).

cases.description: Snapshot provenance.verified is false, so the authority reference cannot be verified either and the snapshot is untrusted. A matching digest does not substitute.
Task needs a command whose allow/deny status depends on the proprietary matcher; no faithful decision is supplied. A textual prefix match with the slot rules does not count.
A declared dependency requires an intermediate human step (a real intermediate human step, not a size heuristic).
cases.mutation: envelope.dependencies = [{id: dep-1, kind: review, step: human}]

cases.description: An independently verified lower bound of 4 mandatory writes exceeds a verified limit of 3. Impossibility rests on the verified mandatory-write lower bound, not on the allowlist size.
cases.mutation: envelope.allowed_files = 4 entries; snapshot.facts.mandatory_writes = known (independent verified source): 4 paths, all inside allowed_files; snapshot.facts.limits = known: max_changed_files 3

cases.description: Four allowed paths against a verified limit of 3, but the independently verified mandatory-write lower bound is 1. allowed_files is permission scope, not required writes, so the allowlist size alone proves nothing.
cases.mutation: envelope.allowed_files = 4 entries; snapshot.facts.mandatory_writes = known (independent verified source): 1 path inside allowed_files; snapshot.facts.limits = known: max_changed_files 3
cases.note: The actual output must still stay inside allowed_files; the requirement does not broaden authority.

cases.description: The envelope's maximum wall budget exceeds a verified runner maximum. That does not prove the task cannot finish earlier, so it is advisory only.
cases.mutation: snapshot.facts.limits = known: max_changed_files 10, max_wall_ms 1800000 (envelope bounds.max_wall_ms stays 3600000)

cases.description: A verified mandatory write is not matched by allowed_files. The allowlist is not widened to cover it.
cases.mutation: snapshot.facts.mandatory_writes = known (independent verified source): [docs/other-146.md] with allowed_files = [docs/example-146.md]

cases.description: No independent verified lower bound exists. A wide allowlist or an upper budget cannot substitute; the bound check is unknown, never fail.
Advisory estimate exceeds the bound, but all trusted checks pass. The estimate neither blocks nor authorizes.

combined_failures.description: Forbidden path + ownership conflict + busy slot + unknown OS identity at once.
combined_failures.proves: highest class wins; all findings retained, ordered by class rank (unauthorized 1, blocked_dependency 2, busy 4, uncertain 5) then check order

combined_failures.description: Busy slot and unknown OS identity.
combined_failures.proves: busy does not hide missing identity; slot.idle (class busy, rank 4) precedes identity.os (class uncertain, rank 5) although it is later in check order and later in bytewise order. reasons is an ordered array, not a lexical set.

combined_failures.description: Unmet automatic dependency and a verified bound exceeded.
Duplicate attempt while fresh, verified evidence of a denied command is individually evaluable.
combined_failures.proves: invalid binding forces uncertain (design default, gate G5) while still reporting the safe evidence; binding class (rank 0) sorts before unauthorized (rank 1)

combined_failures.description: The snapshot is stale and its decision said denied. Stale evidence must not pose as a proven denial: authority.commands is stale, not fail, and appears once (not duplicated by the expansion).
combined_failures.mutation: evaluated_at_ms = 1789999950000 (after the snapshot window end 1789999900000, before the envelope expiry 1790000000000); snapshot.facts.command_decisions = known: cmd:git-diff-check=denied
combined_failures.proves: stale evidence cannot yield unauthorized; binding.not_expired still passes because the envelope has not expired

combined_failures.description: Stale epoch and envelope expiry together, with the snapshot window extended so freshness is not the cause.
combined_failures.proves: binding failures are all listed in check order; a wrong-epoch snapshot is not evaluable (not stale) even though it is also past some window

consumption_cases.contract: These cases belong to validate_report_for_consumption(report, envelope, snapshot, nowMs) (design doc 6.1), NOT to evaluate(envelope, snapshot, nowMs), which has no prior report. They validate a prior report bound to the baseline: task_digest = design vector B digest, capability_digest = digest:cap-A-rev-3, capability_revision = 3, report expires_at_ms = 1789999900000 (min of envelope and snapshot expiry). valid:true means only 'this report describes exactly these inputs and is unexpired'; it never authorizes, never proves the facts still hold, and does not close TOCTOU.
consumption_cases.baseline_presented: Presented envelope is the baseline (digest matches), presented snapshot is the baseline (digest digest:cap-A-rev-3, revision 3, verified), nowMs = 1789999500000.

cases.description: Everything matches and the report is unexpired.

Task unchanged. A different, still-fresh snapshot of the same slot and same epoch is presented (a fact changed, so its digest is digest:cap-A-rev-4 and its revision is 4). consume.task_digest and report freshness pass; the capability binding fails.
cases.mutation: presented snapshot = same slot slot-x, epoch 7, revision 4, captured_at_ms 1789999400000, expires_at_ms 1790000100000, one fact changed, provenance verified; nowMs = 1789999500000
cases.note: Not stale, not expired, task digest equal: distinct from report_expired and from task_digest_drift. A fresh evaluate() is required; the old report is not consumable.

cases.description: The envelope presented at consumption differs from the one the report bound (any byte change, for example allowed_files).
cases.mutation: presented envelope allowed_files changed; digest != report.task_digest

cases.description: Same inputs, but the consumer checks after the report's expires_at_ms. Expiry is a time condition (stale), distinct from a digest mismatch (fail).
A member of the stored report was altered; recomputing the digest over the report bytes without the report_digest member does not equal the stored report_digest. Self-field exclusion is explicit.
cases.mutation: report.verdict edited after the fact; stored report_digest unchanged

cases.description: Digests and revision match, but the presented snapshot's provenance.verified is false. A hash match is never authority or trust.
cases.mutation: presented snapshot provenance.verified = false (digest assumed equal for illustration)

proposals.status: ACCEPTED DESIGN (design doc section 13; operator accepted all proposed choices, gate G9 resolved). Group key 'proposals' is kept only for traceability to PR #170. Illustrative only: NOT implemented, not executable readiness proof, no conformance measurement; acceptance authorizes no evaluator/consumption implementation (G8 not started). Every case names the contract it illustrates; none of it changes the published design vectors A/B. 'alternative'/'alternatives' entries are NOT SELECTED historical alternatives, not pending defaults.
proposals.provenance_note: All facts are injected synthetic claims for pure tests. 'verified' is a declaration, not a runtime grant. Digests are symbolic labels.

proposed_schema_baseline.status: ACCEPTED SCHEMA BASELINE (design only, illustrative, not executable). Separate from the legacy summary baseline above; use this for closed-schema cases.
proposed_schema_baseline.description: A future proposed schema baseline, separate from the legacy baseline. Its envelope body is byte-identical to the legacy baseline envelope (design vector B, sha256 43e77d4fafa97cc56fe831d1bdcb145468f821b940bdf1519a074157c9527880), and its allowed_files pattern 'docs/example-146.md' is a valid A1 exact path. The snapshot differs from the legacy summary (closed value schemas plus artifact_contract and authority_decision), so its digest is symbolic and is NOT claimed to equal any legacy digest.
proposed_schema_baseline.traceability: Legacy case ids (allowed_small_task, forbidden_path, ...) remain defined only against the legacy baseline above; proposal cases below carry a legacy_case reference where a counterpart exists.

pattern_validity.result: valid terminal alias, same meaning as docs/

matching.note: forbidden descendant inside allowed directory blocks
dir/dir ancestor; also checked in reverse order (design doc 13.1)

intersection.rule: Normal form after the alias step (terminal /** removed BEFORE the no-star segment grammar): (kind exact|dir, segs). exact/exact: segs equal. exact/dir: dir segs are a PROPER prefix of the exact segs. dir/dir: one segs is a prefix of the other (equal counts). Exact is a leaf: never a prefix of anything; exact a and dir a/ are disjoint.

cases.why: exact a is a leaf, not a prefix of a/b
equal segments, exact vs directory: a/ excludes a itself
exact a/b is a member of a/
alias a/** is a/ after the alias step
exact a is a leaf; it is not inside a/b/ and a/b/ is not inside a

alternatives.A1-alt-2: defer grammar: any non-exact pattern makes authority.paths unknown (path_pattern_unsupported, not an accepted code); with allowed_files ['docs/'] the verdict is uncertain.

Omitted facts are never normalized into invented timestamps, digests or values.

cases.note: Not identity_os_unknown: no report exists.

cases.note: TaskEnvelope.dependencies stays an ordered array; no sort, no dedup, no identity validation unless separately proposed.

object_set.alternative: NOT SELECTED, OS-alt: no object-set schema; duplicates are still rejected by an explicit uniqueness check, but object-entry arrays are not order-checked, so unsorted_set is no longer produced for object-entry arrays (command_decisions/dependencies/fixtures entries). unsorted_set stays valid for STRING sets (attempts_seen.ids, path_policy.forbidden, mandatory_writes.paths, envelope string sets). The actual cost: equal abstract entry sets emitted in different orders produce different capability digests.

ownership_files_combination.expectation_status: ACCEPTED DESIGN (A3); illustrative, not executed. Per-reason class is the accepted reading; the not-selected alternative follows.
ownership_files_combination.rule: Known failure (worktree.clean false OR ownership.conflict true) -> check fail, blocked_dependency. Else any unavailable (status unknown/absent) -> check unknown. Else both known ok -> pass. All applicable codes retained; check reason_codes ascending bytewise. reasons[] sort key unchanged (class rank, check order, code) with per-reason class: worktree_dirty/ownership_conflict = blocked_dependency (2); worktree_unknown/ownership_unknown = uncertain (5) even when the check status is fail.

cases.note: known failure kept distinct from unavailable evidence; check status fixed to fail; reasons[] ordered by class rank, check_reason_codes ordered by code.

ownership_files_combination.alternative_A3_alt_owner: NOT SELECTED historical alternative. Keep the class rule strictly per check status: same check status and same codes, but every reason of a fail check has class blocked_dependency, so o_dirty_unknown_owner lists ownership.files:ownership_unknown before ownership.files:worktree_dirty and o_conflict_unknown_worktree keeps ownership_conflict before worktree_unknown (both by code). section 6 item 4 is unchanged under this alternative. A lossy variant that drops the unavailable reasons is rejected.

a3_artifact_and_worktree.alternative: NOT SELECTED, A3-alt: no artifact_contract/worktree facts; contract.artifact is always unknown, so every case is uncertain with contract.artifact:artifact_evidence_unknown.

cases.description: The presented report has an unusable identity and digest (task_id is not a string, report_digest is not 64 hex). None of its fields are read or echoed.
cases.note: report_not_evaluable is not a digest or revision mismatch.
Schema-valid report: all eight checks run; mismatch is distinct from expiry.

a6_malformed_report_consumption.alternative: NOT SELECTED, A6-alt: a schema-invalid report would make validate_report_for_consumption throw FeasibilityInputError (input: report). Accepted A6: a ConsumptionResult with valid=false, consume.report_schema fail report_schema_invalid, and seven checks unknown report_not_evaluable.

proposals.snapshot_derived_list_note: Accepted list = the 13 entries of meta.snapshot_derived_checks, in check order: authority.reference, authority.paths, authority.commands, identity.os, permission.profile, matcher.compat, repo.base, ownership.files, contract.artifact, dependency.declared, fixtures.data, slot.idle, bounds.explicit (history: the pre-acceptance list had 11, without authority.reference and contract.artifact). binding.* checks and estimate.advisory are never in the list. Evidence dependencies: authority.paths<-path_policy,mandatory_writes; authority.commands<-command_decisions; identity.os<-os_identity; permission.profile<-permission_profile; matcher.compat<-permission_profile,command_decisions; repo.base<-repo_base; ownership.files<-ownership(+worktree, A3); contract.artifact<-artifact_contract (A3); authority.reference<-authority_decision (A4); dependency.declared<-dependencies; fixtures.data<-fixtures; slot.idle<-slot_state; bounds.explicit<-limits,mandatory_writes; binding.attempt_unique<-attempts_seen.

snapshot_derived_expansion.expectation_status: ACCEPTED DESIGN (A3+A4); illustrative, not executed. The legacy cases carry the same 13-entry expansion (see meta.superseded_illustrative_expectations).
snapshot_derived_expansion.note: Each adopted check appears exactly once; an explicit reason for a check IS its entry (authority.reference:authority_unverified is not repeated as evidence_not_evaluable). Order: binding entries (rank 0), then uncertain class by check order.

properties.statement: Two evaluations of the same (envelope, snapshot, evaluated_at_ms) produce byte-identical MCTL-CJ1 output and the same report_digest, also when input object key insertion order differs.

reasons[] is an ordered array sorted by (class rank, check order, code), never a bytewise-sorted set. The encoder never sorts or de-duplicates it, and the evaluator emits each (check, code) at most once.

Changing any snapshot fact changes capability_digest. validate_report_for_consumption (not evaluate) rejects a report bound to the old capability_digest and revision against the new snapshot with capability_digest_mismatch and capability_revision_mismatch, even when the new snapshot is still fresh, same-epoch, and the task digest is unchanged. Expiry (report_expired, stale) and mismatch (fail) use different codes.

Output contains only closed-enum strings and schema-validated identifiers. It never contains credentials, tokens, absolute or private filesystem paths, host names, message/question text, tool output or task prose.
Evaluation and consumption validation perform no store write, send, ack, reservation, commit, push, PR, worktree write, subprocess, network call, clock read or random read.
verdict is feasible only if binding_valid is true and every required check has status pass. unknown, absent and stale are never read as pass.

A feasible report and a valid consumption result carry or imply non_claims not_authorization, not_reservation, not_os_isolation, not_toctou_closure; none of them is ever absent or false. Digests bind inputs and are never authority.
absent (does not exist), unknown (not determinable or not faithfully evaluable) and fail (evaluated and not met) produce different check statuses and different reason codes.

needs_split from size requires an independently verified lower bound of mandatory writes exceeding a verified limit, or a real human step. A wide allowed_files, a large upper budget or a pessimistic estimate alone never does. Required writes never widen allowed_files.
